exclusions_stated_by_publisher: Case reports involving domestic violence are not reported (doc_00.json description).
Case reports involving child abuse are not reported (doc_00.json description).
Case reports involving sex offenses involving minors are not reported (doc_00.json description).

Only incidents that result in a police report being generated by the responding officer are included (doc_00.json description: 'Police Cases represent all police incidents that result in a police report being generated').
known_differences_from_fetch_script: Unit: one row per case with a single 'case' type (raw_cache_profile.json: casenumber distinct_count 109632 = rows 109632). The FBI counts every Part I offense in an incident (NIBRS) or the highest under the hierarchy rule (SRS); here each case carries only the one type the publisher assigned, so offenses secondary to a case's type are not counted.

Domestic violence cases are withheld by the publisher (doc_00.json), so aggravated assault, rape, robbery and murder are undercounted relative to the official totals. 2018-2025 mapped rows vs official_totals.csv sums: aggravated_assault 1484 vs 1831, rape 226 vs 379, robbery 718 vs 736, murder 44 vs 51.

Sex offenses involving minors are withheld (doc_00.json), yet the category is 'RAPE/RAPE OF CHILD' (227 rows); the remaining rows cannot be split into adult and child victims, and statutory rape of a child may not meet the FBI rape definition (11A/11B/11C).

'ASSAULT - FELONY' (1486 rows) is the publisher's felony/misdemeanor split, not the FBI aggravated/simple split: Washington felony assault (1st-3rd degree) includes some assaults without a weapon or serious injury (e.g., 3rd-degree assault on officers), which the FBI counts as simple assault, while 'MISDEMEANOR ASSAULT' (5794 rows) is left unmapped.

'HOMICIDE' (44 rows) cannot be separated into murder (09A), negligent manslaughter (09B) and justifiable homicide (09C); 'DEATH INVESTIGATION' (2062 rows) is left unmapped though some may later be reclassified as murder.

Larceny maps 'THEFT - MISDEMEANOR', 'THEFT - FELONY', 'VEHICLE PROWL - MISDEMEANOR' and 'VEHICLE PROWL - FELONY' (20479 rows; 20410 after the unfounded exclusion) vs 21731 official. 'IDENTITY THEFT', 'FRAUD - FORGERY - UIBC', 'PSP/TSP - FELONY'/'PSP/TSP - MISD' (possession of stolen property) and 'RECOV OF OTHER AGENCY STOLEN' are not larceny under the FBI definitions and stay unmapped.

Motor vehicle theft maps 'VEHICLE THEFT' and 'MOTOR VEHICLE W/O PERMISSION' (6372 rows; 6318 after the unfounded exclusion) vs 6629 official; 'RECOV OF OTHER AGENCY STOLEN' (2592) is another agency's theft and stays unmapped.
Dates are the report/initiation time (datetimereceived), not occurrence time; the feed publishes no occurrence date.
Attempted offenses are kept (attemptedstatus ATTEMPTED 1543 rows overall), as the FBI counts attempts for these offenses; the rules do not filter on attemptedstatus.

Rows with disposition 'UNFOUNDED' or 'NO CRIME OCCURRED' are excluded to approximate the FBI's unfounded exclusion (131 mapped rows: 20479-20410 larceny, 6372-6318 MVT, 4672-4668 burglary, 1486-1484 aggravated assault, 227-226 rape, 719-718 robbery); other dispositions and sealed/expunged cases are kept.
notes: One row per case: casenumber is unique in the pull (raw_cache_profile.json: distinct_count 109632 of 109632 rows), so id_fields [casenumber] with dedupe_on_id keeps one row per incident; each case carries one publisher-assigned 'case' type, so there is no multi-offense choice to make. Date: datetimereceived, which doc_00.json defines as the date and time the incident 'was reported or initiated by police' - a report date; no occurrence date is published. caseyear equals the year of datetimereceived on every row (query: 0 mismatches), so year_field is left empty and the year comes from datetimereceived. Range in the pull 2018-01-01T00:07:25 to 2025-12-31T23:20:05. The where clause is the registry probe_where, which is the filter the archive was pulled under (packet.json case_text); order ':id' is the registry probe_order; page_size 50000 (registry blank). Coordinates: geomcoordinate is a GeoJSON Point (doc_00.json 'Point plot for the approximate incident location'), read with geomcoordinate#point; 675 rows have no point and are dropped by require_coordinates (79 of them among mapped rows kept after the unfounded exclusion: 1484-1482 aggravated assault, 4668-4666 burglary, 20410-20348 larceny, 6318-6316 MVT, 226-216 rape, 718-717 robbery, 44-44 murder, by query on raw_cache). The publisher rounds addresses to the 100 block (doc_00.json occurredlocationby100block description), and the points are coarser still: 1987 distinct points for 22360 distinct 100-block addresses (query on raw_cache), e.g. one point [-122.234563, 47.915308] carries 3335 rows across 579 addresses on E/W Casino Rd, so points are approximate location centroids and block-group assignment near block-group edges is uncertain. 631 rows fall outside a rough Everett box (lat 47.85-48.05, lon -122.32 to -122.12; point range lat 47.41-48.44, lon -122.38 to -121.34), which the scope footprint will drop. Offense mapping checked against the pull's distinct 'case' values (raw_cache_profile.json): HOMICIDE 44 -> murder; RAPE/RAPE OF CHILD 227 -> rape; ROBBERY 719 -> robbery; ASSAULT - FELONY 1486 -> aggravated_assault; BURGLARY 4672 -> burglary; THEFT - MISDEMEANOR 14107 + THEFT - FELONY 4438 + VEHICLE PROWL - MISDEMEANOR 1612 + VEHICLE PROWL - FELONY 322 -> larceny; VEHICLE THEFT 6331 + MOTOR VEHICLE W/O PERMISSION 41 -> motor_vehicle_theft. No NIBRS codes are published. 2018-2025 mapped rows after the unfounded exclusion vs official_totals.csv 8-year sums (summed by hand from the file): murder 44 vs 51, rape 226 vs 379, robbery 718 vs 736, aggravated_assault 1484 vs 1831, burglary 4668 vs 4687, larceny 20410 vs 21731, motor_vehicle_theft 6318 vs 6629. Per-year raw counts by type were checked (e.g. 2018 burglary 638 vs 661, larceny 1975+607+338+70=2990 vs 3120, MVT 942+12=954 vs 963).
